# Linda Bramsen

Linda Bramsen is a leading senior consultant physician (*ledende overlæge*) in Child and Adolescent Psychiatry (*Børne- og Ungdomspsykiatrien*) in Region Nordjylland, Denmark [^src1][^src2]. She serves as a representative for Region Nordjylland (RN) [^src1] and is listed as a member of the steering group for the Danish ADHD database, a national health quality-registry that monitors the diagnosis and treatment of ADHD in children and adolescents under 18 [^src1][^src2].

Bramsen appears in the steering group membership listings of two consecutive annual reports on the ADHD database — the 2023 report and the 2024 report — in both cases identified with the same professional role and regional affiliation [^src1][^src2]. In the 2024 listing, her entry additionally notes an association with the *Børne- og Ungdomspsykiatrisk Selskab i Danmark* (the Danish Child and Adolescent Psychiatric Society) [^src2]. The steering group she belongs to is described as drawing together senior consultants, specialist physicians, psychologists, nurses, epidemiologists and relative/patient representatives from across Denmark, reflecting all five Danish regions, relevant professional societies, patient organizations, and the Danish Healthcare Quality Programme (Sundhedsvæsenets Kvalitetsinstitut) [^src1][^src2]. In this broader context, the database itself tracks statistics on the population of children and young people assessed or treated for ADHD, including findings such as markedly lower rates of children with ADHD passing the lower-secondary school leaving exam before age 17 compared with the general population [^src1].

Her role connects her directly to [[region-nordjylland|Region Nordjylland]], the regional health authority she both works for and represents on the national steering group [^src1][^src2].
